item.title: Python asyncio in 2026: A Practical Guide to Async/Await
item.description: I spent my first few weeks with asyncio writing code that looked async but ran exactly like synchronous code — one await at a time, zero concurrency gained, and no error telling me why. The syntax is deceptively simple; the mental model underneath it is not. This is the guide I wish I’d had: what the event loop actually does, how async/await really behaves, and the specific mistakes that make people give up on asyncio and reach for threads instead.
